data.name: Magical Letterbox
data.description:
The Magical Letterbox is a post box that, when supplied with a coin, summons a Courier to carry letters placed within it.
Bronn Boromir used the Letterbox to send a message to his uncle Bogo Boromir by inserting a gold coin. A Courier appeared, retrieved the party's earlier undelivered parcels and loose acorns, took Bronn's new letter, and departed down the mountain carrying all the items.

data.name: Hang Gliders
data.description: Hang Gliders are canvas-and-frame flying rigs located in a cavern, leaning against the wall next to a pile of dead adventurers. The Hang Gliders were used to jump from a mountain hole, allowing users to glide down through tundra amid violent winds and snow-covered peaks, ultimately landing in a Farmer's Field Beside Byriver adjacent to By River, where smoke and the sound of a dragon's roar were present.

data.name: Dragon-Sized Bowl Of Chamomile Tea
data.description:
The Dragon-Sized Bowl Of Chamomile Tea is a large bowl containing cold chamomile tea, equipped with an oversized tea bag and a small, human-sized teaspoon that is scarred and singed, identified as Dookeldorn Bludvart's brother's teaspoon.
The bowl was discovered in the dragon's Hoard (About Five Thousand Gold) chamber next to the wounded, sleeping Haldraxis. Dookeldorn recognized the teaspoon, confirming his brother's fate, which led him to summon his companion Pepe. The party decided to return to the cave to claim the Hoard that included the bowl.

data.name: Distinctive Handkerchief
data.description: Distinctive Handkerchief is a relic known as Dookeldorn Bludvart’s brother’s handkerchief and is described as Pepe’s favorite handkerchief used to catch bodily fluids. It was retrieved intact but soaked from Haldraxis’s corpse after the dragon's death; its pattern was barely discernible at the time of recovery.

data.name: Scorched Teaspoon
data.description:
Scorched Teaspoon is a human-sized teaspoon, scarred and singed, identified as belonging to Dookeldorn Bludvart's brother. It was found in Haldraxis's dragon-sized bowl of chamomile in the Hoard (About Five Thousand Gold) chamber.
Dookeldorn recognized the His Brother's Scorched Teaspoon while entering the Hoard chamber, which confirmed his brother's death and prompted him to call forth his small dragon companion, Pepe.

data.name: Ice-Flower Petals
data.description:
Ice-Flower Petals are consumable ice flowers utilized as cold-effect projectiles. They can be held in quantities of eight or thirteen and can be affixed to a crossbow bolt. A mage hand can carry twenty-one petals, which can deal twenty-one cold damage.
In a recorded event, a party planned to deliver petals into Haldraxis's gizzard. Bronn Boromir, using a mage hand, launched a bundled set of twenty-one Ice-Flower Petals into the dragon's wounded throat. Frost spread across the dragon's flesh, briefly evaporated, and more blood seeped through the bandages.

data.name: Hoard (About Five Thousand Gold)
data.description: Hoard (About Five Thousand Gold) is a collection of coin and treasure located in Haldraxis's Hoard Chamber, quantified as approximately five thousand gold. The Hoard was discovered when a group entered the chamber and found it unusually small for a dragon's trove, described as "not nearly enough" for Haldraxis. The group noted they would return to the cave to claim the Hoard.

data.name: Philip’s Map
data.description: Philip’s Map is a detailed map provided by Philip, outlining the route through the mountain pass to the ancient ruins where Haldraxis meets for extortion payments. The map was used to reach the Old Temple Ruins located above By River.

data.name: Stone Tablets
data.description: Stone Tablets are three small circular Stone Tablets set vertically in a stone-blocked western door. Two tablets were already in place, and one matching Dragon-Head Medallion was found near a giant bedroll. The Stone Tablets include a tablet bearing a claw image and a separate Dragon-Head Tablet that was inserted into the remaining slot. The tablets were rearranged into the correct order, with the dragon head above the claw and the tail below. When placed and ordered correctly, the stone door rumbled open, revealing the Treasure Chamber and the sleeping, wounded Haldraxis.

data.name: Cache Of Ice Flowers
data.description: Cache Of Ice Flowers is a prepared cache containing ten Ice Flowers, gathered and held by Bronn Boromir. Bronn hurled the cache with a telekinetic mage hand at Haldraxis, causing the flowers to detonate in succession and create a burst of frost. The frost coated surfaces and inflicted pain and rock-solid damage to Haldraxis. Bronn used ten flowers in the attack. One flower from the cache was later consumed by E.t. Skittles.

data.name: Dragon-Head Medallion
data.description:
The Dragon-Head Medallion is a large circular stone disk etched with a relief image of a dragon's head. Its edges are shaped to fit into a larger mechanism.
The medallion was discovered in a Sleeping Area. It was inspected by E.t. Skittles, who noted its fit for a specific purpose. The group later placed the Dragon-Head Tablet into a slot of a stone-blocked door that had three vertical circular tablet slots. Once inserted and the tablets reordered, the stone door rumbled open, revealing the Treasure Chamber.

data.name: Cube Of Force
data.description:
The Cube Of Force is a small portable cube created by E.t. Skittles. It projects a fifteen-foot cubic barrier around its user and nearby individuals. The barrier blocks the passage of creatures and hostile effects at E.t.’s discretion while allowing walls, floors, and ceilings to pass. It prevents attacks or actions from within and cannot be exited until E.t. drops it. The cube protects against steam and fire, reducing fire damage by 1d10.
E.t. produced the Cube Of Force at the mountain skull entrance, gathered the party inside the cube, and used its barrier to allow the group to walk through scalding steam without harm. The party remained sheltered until the cube was dropped, after which they continued into the Mist-Filled Foyer and proceeded to the northwest door.

data.name: Troll Fat
data.description:
Troll Fat: rendered fat taken from trolls kept by the party, used as a stored food or bait item.
Chronology: Dookeldorn Bludvart placed Troll Fat at the cave mouth, where it was hit by steaming blasts. The steam seared and caramelized the fat, producing a strong, appetizing smell that drew attention from deeper in Mountainside Cave Carved Like An Enormous Dragon Skull. Later, after killing a giant, the party harvested additional Troll Fat from the giant's remains.

data.name: Looted Giant Camp Journal
data.description:
Giant Camp Journal is a journal recovered from a looted mountain Looted Giant Camp.
The journal records that the Mountain Giants hated By River, that their interests with Haldraxis were aligned and had progressed into active cooperation, and that at least one giant had moved into Haldraxis' new headquarters or lair.

data.name: Tiny Crayon-Written Manifesto
data.description:
Tiny Crayon-Written Manifesto: A small booklet, scrawled in crayon, discovered on a slain mountain giant. The writing is crude and filled with errors, presenting itself as a manifesto.
The manifesto expresses anger toward the people of Byriver, claiming that knights from By River came to address the "mountain giant problem." It calls for the giants to retaliate against By River and includes references to Haldraxis, noting the giants' interactions with the red dragon.

data.name: Tarp-Wrapped Hovering Object
data.description:
Tarp-Wrapped Hovering Object: a canvas- or tarp-wrapped item that hovered beside Dookeldorn Bludvart in his corner booth, covered in thick cloth to conceal its contents.
It remained beside him while he sulked at the bar. Dookeldorn later referred to it as "this package" and unwrapped it to reveal a Moonbow. He then grabbed the tarp-wrapped package and set out immediately on the Mountain Route.

data.name: Magical Ice Flowers
data.description:
Magical Ice Flowers are blue-white blooms with petals that are cold to the touch and possess magical properties that can be beneficial or harmful. They can be harvested intact and must be packed gently to avoid being crushed.
The party discovered a meadow of Ice Flowers on a mountain. Dookeldorn Bludvart plucked some and later stepped on crushed flowers, experiencing a painful burst of cold. The group harvested twenty-six intact flowers. Bronn Boromir consumed one and gained vitality, while Dookeldorn ate one to recover from a cold burn. E.t. Skittles wove some into a decorative lei. Additional Ice Flowers were later found around a giant encampment.

data.name: Moonbow
data.description: Moonbow is a glimmering bow created by Dookeldorn Bludvart. Dookeldorn claimed it is his brother's most valuable possession and stated that the bow generates its own ammunition. During its first use on the mountain, Dookeldorn experienced a critical failure; the bow's light flickered, and he failed to control its special effect, which produced a mystical dim light on the target, granting advantage to the next attack. Later, he successfully fired the Glimmering Moonbow again and killed a fleeing mountain giant.
